summary: Part of it is a normal setting; the rest lives behind chrome://flags, where you have to hunt a dozen separate AI entries. New Chrome releases keep adding flags that default to enabled.

steps.path: Chrome → ⋮ → Settings → System → toggle off "On device AI"; then Settings → AI Innovations → Gemini in Chrome → toggle everything off
Open chrome://flags, search "AI" then "Gemini", and set each match to Disabled. Minimum set:
steps.code:
AI Mode Omnibox entrypoint → Disabled
AI Entrypoint Disabled on User Input → Disabled
Omnibox Allow AI Mode Matches → Disabled
Prompt API for Gemini Nano → Disabled
Prompt API for Gemini Nano with Multimodal Input → Disabled

steps.path: Fleet-wide: use Chrome Enterprise policies (GenAI* policies) instead of flags — flags reset on channel updates.

collateral: flags are per-profile and can be reset by an update
each Chrome release adds new AI flags you have to re-audit
disabling on-device AI also disables non-Gemini local ML features
whyTheyDidIt: The browser is where Google most needs Gemini to become a habit before someone else's assistant does.
